title: Copilot Studio: interactive MCP apps render inside agent conversations
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, rendering behaviour, billing statements and control paths are supported. The updated governance documentation still limits enforcement to supported management routes, consistent with the briefing's caution about MCP app-originated calls.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The server-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: The beta package block operation is POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking an MCP server disables all its exposed tools through the supported governance route.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes. This action targets the server component, rather than a whole plugin package.

claims.claim: Server-blocking controls are not explicitly confirmed to apply to MCP app-originated calls.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP apps Agent 365 Tooling Gateway block app tools call enforcement. Read mcp-apps, manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and azure/api-management/agent-365; enforcement covers governed routes, not all products, with no specific app-call confirmation.

claims.claim: The beta package block API is subject to change and not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: block and reject API licensing
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block operation requires delegated work-or-school CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |
| Application | Not available. | Not available. |

claims.claim: The package block operation takes no request body.
claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Individual tool toggles are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled or Disabled toggle > Save.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle.

claims.claim: No administrator-facing API call for the individual MCP tool enable/disable control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 MCP individual tool enabled disabled granular control API Graph gateway tools policy; individual MCP tool block automation API policy PUT. Read Package API overview, manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and Azure Agent 365 guidance; no equivalent call.

claims.claim: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants

claims.claim: Individual tool controls support only specific MCP server types registered on Agent 365.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Individual tool enforcement is not explicitly confirmed for MCP app-originated calls.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP apps Agent 365 Tooling Gateway block app tools call enforcement. Read mcp-apps and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers: supported gateway experiences are covered, but applicability across products and app-originated calls is not stated.

claims.claim: Developer MCP registration requests are reviewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Requests (preview) > request > Approve or Reject.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Requests (preview)** tab. Review the server name, publisher, requester, and request date. Select **Approve** to make the server available in the organizational registry, or **Reject** to deny the request.

claims.claim: A pending staged package submission can be rejected with POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject.
claims.quote:
Reject a pending Copilot package title submission.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: AI Administrator meets the permissions requirements for the MCP review and approval process.
claims.quote:
Two roles meet both requirements:
- AI Administrator.
- Global Administrator.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Global Administrator also meets the permissions requirements for the MCP review and approval process.

Two roles meet both requirements:

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra consent is a separate step after MCP registration approval.
claims.quote: Granting the required Microsoft Entra consent is a separate step. After approval, consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions required by the MCP server.

claims.claim: The reject API reviews a pending title submission rather than approving a request or granting consent.
claims.quote: Reject a pending Copilot package title submission. This action reviews a package title and its submitted version; it doesn't reject an individual user's request.

claims.claim: The reject request should supply the matching staged submission version in the version body property.
claims.quote:
Supply the version of the staged submission you're rejecting.
| `version` | String | Version of the staged package title submission to reject. Optional in the schema; use the matching submitted version to target a specific review. |

claims.claim: The data policy path uses Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy, environment selection, Assign connectors and the connector's three dots > Block.
claims.quote: On the sidebar, select **Security**, and then select **Data and privacy**. Select **Data policy**. Select **New Policy**. The **Add an environment** page appears. The **Assign connectors** page appears. Select the three dots (**⋮**) next to the connector

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <connector-objects> places connectors in a DLP policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]>
Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).
The policy name (GUID).

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy moves connectors already classified elsewhere into the specified group.
claims.quote: If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.claim: Every connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy must contain id.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- id: The unique identifier of the connector.

claims.claim: Every connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy must contain type.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- type: The type of the connector

claims.claim: Every connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy must contain name.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.claim: Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in environments included in the policy's scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The data policy page does not specifically mention MCP apps.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP apps Agent 365 Tooling Gateway block app tools call enforcement; read Configure data policies for agents, including its scope and MCP connector passage. The page names MCP servers but not MCP apps; its general policy reach remains documented.

claims.claim: The tenant tools registry can be inventoried at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry.
claims.quote:
Use the **Registry** tab to discover and manage tools available in your tenant.
In the left navigation pane, select **Agents** > **Tools** > **Registry**.

claims.claim: The standard-harness MCP overview says tool changes on the server are reflected dynamically.
claims.quote: When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness how-to says to edit the server entry to refresh the connection and re-read changed exposed tools.
claims.quote: If a server's URL, authentication, or exposed tools change after you add it, edit the server entry in the same **Tools** dialog to refresh the connection and re-read the tool list.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness MCP server how-to is prerelease documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The sources do not state that existing agents automatically change when this feature arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP apps tenant default existing agents automatic rendering admin switch. Read roadmap, mcp-apps and tools-add-mcp-server; they describe connected UI-enabled tools but do not state a change automatically applied to existing agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center provides controls for plugins, skills and MCP servers.
claims.quote: This article explains how to upload, install, uninstall, and delete plugins and skills; manage plugin availability; review access requests; and govern MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Power Platform data policies control which tools makers can add in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Power Platform data policies still control which tools makers can add in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Agent 365 and Copilot Studio can have separate controls, so blocking in one is not documented as universally blocking in the other.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.where: Governance controls: data policy completion instructions
claims.claim: After Block, the data policy procedure uses Next, Define scope if prompted, Next, review and Create policy.
claims.quote: Select **Next**. If you're a tenant admin, or an environment admin for multiple environments, the **Define scope** page opens. Select **Next**. Review your policy, and then select **Create policy** if you're creating a new policy

claims.quote: Replace `{packageId}` with the title ID confirmed for reviewing the pending submission.

claims.claim: The reject operation must not use an individual request identifier as its target.
claims.quote: Don't substitute an individual request identifier.

claims.claim: The reject API is beta and not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |

claims.claim: The Package Management API represents tools such as MCP servers in the organization catalog and supports their administrative review and blocking.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. Admin reviews pending requests for MCP servers. Admin blocks a package to prevent its usage across the organization.
